– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- The failing test constructs a format without an explicit record separator:
  CSVFormat.newFormat(';').withSkipHeaderRecord(true).withHeader("H1", "H2")

- Implementation pathway:
  - CSVFormat.format(Object...) creates a StringWriter and delegates to new CSVPrinter(out, this).printRecord(values), then returns out.toString().trim().
  - CSVPrinter.printRecord(Object...) prints each value via print(value) and then calls println().

- Printing the values:
  - The first value "A" is written without a delimiter because newRecord is initially true.
  - The second value "B" is written with the delimiter ';' because newRecord becomes false after the first value.

- Appending the record separator:
  - CSVPrinter.println() does:
    final String recordSeparator = format.getRecordSeparator();
    out.append(recordSeparator);
  - CSVFormat.getRecordSeparator() returns the field recordSeparator.
  - CSVFormat.newFormat(char) constructs a CSVFormat with recordSeparator set to null.

- Root cause:
  - When recordSeparator is null, out.append(recordSeparator) is invoked with a null CharSequence. Per the JDK Appendable contract (and StringWriter’s implementation), appending a null CharSequence writes the literal string "null".
  - As a result, the formatted output becomes "A;Bnull".
  - CSVFormat.format(...).trim() does not remove "null" (only leading/trailing whitespace), so the final string still incorrectly ends with "null".

- Conclusion:
  - The bug is that CSVPrinter.println() unconditionally appends the record separator without handling the case where it is null. With the default from CSVFormat.newFormat(char), recordSeparator is null, leading to "null" being appended.
  - The expected behavior (per the test and bug report) is that no record separator should be appended when it is not configured, yielding "A;B" instead of "A;Bnull".

- Suggested fix direction:
  - In CSVPrinter.println(), check for a null record separator and either:
    - do not append anything when it is null, or
    - use a sensible default line separator if that aligns with library design.
  - Alternatively, ensure CSVFormat.newFormat(char) sets a non-null default record separator, but the minimal, localized fix is to guard against null in println().

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
